rejected.title: Threats to food security
card: Food security needs enough food to be available and people to be able to get it. A threat is anything that reduces the supply of food or stops people from getting it.
Supply threats

Drought, climate change and land degradation can cut how much food farms produce. Land degradation is the loss of soil quality, so land grows less. Food waste means food that is grown but never eaten.
Access threats
Poverty can leave people unable to afford food. Rising prices make food cost more. Conflict can destroy farms and block food from reaching people.
Threats often act together. For example, a drought can cut harvests, which can push prices up, and poor families are hit first.
rejected.remember: Threats can cut the supply of food or stop people getting it, and they often act together.

a.q: Supermarkets near Mai's home in Wollongong are well stocked, and food prices have not changed. Since her parent lost a job, her family cannot buy enough food. Which threat explains this?
opts: Poverty, as the family can no longer afford food
Rising prices, as food now costs the family more
Drought, as nearby farms are growing less food
Land degradation, as the soil now grows less food
a.why: The shops have plenty of food and prices are the same, so the problem is access: the family has less money to buy food. Rising prices is tempting, but the case says prices have not changed. Drought and land degradation cut supply, and supply here is fine.
a.clue: Is the problem the food in the shops, or the family's money?

b.q: A region in East Africa has a long drought, and then fighting breaks out. Farms are abandoned and food prices climb. Which statement best describes what is happening?
opts: Several threats are acting together to reduce food security
Only drought is a threat, as conflict does not affect food
Food security is unaffected, as prices decide supply
The region has a food waste problem, not a supply problem
b.why: Drought can cut harvests and conflict can stop farming and block food, while higher prices make food harder to afford. These threats act together. Food waste is a different threat and is not described in the case.
b.clue: Count how many threats the scenario describes.

flags: Question b, level: The wrong options are weak and easy to rule out (food waste is not mentioned, and 'prices decide supply' does not make sense). A student can pick the right answer without understanding how threats combine.

a.q: Which of these is a threat to food security because it makes food harder to afford?
opts: Rising food prices
Crop rotation on farms
A good wheat harvest
Efficient irrigation
a.why: Rising prices make food cost more, so poorer people may not be able to buy enough. The other options help produce food or describe plentiful supply, so they do not make food harder to afford.
a.clue: Which option makes food cost more?
